# Jubilees Chapter 18 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 18:2 — "high land" vs. "high country" vs. "highland"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "go into the high land" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "go to the high land" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "go to the high country" | More natural |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS "high land." All three are close; "high land" follows the Ge'ez compound noun directly. "High country" (PNEUMA) is colloquial; the destination is a specific elevated territory.

---

## 18:11-12 — First-person narration at the climax

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "And I called unto him from heaven... And I said" | Archaic with "unto" |
| LOGOS | "And I called to him from heaven... And I said" | Modern formal — "to him" |
| PNEUMA | "I called out to him from heaven... I said" | Drops "And" connectors |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "And I called to him from heaven" preserves the connective "And" which has structural weight here — it marks the angel's entry at the critical moment. PNEUMA's dropping of "And" makes the passage feel like independent clauses rather than a climactic continuation.

---

## 18:14 — Naming of the place: "Jehovah-jireh" vs. "The LORD will provide"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "The LORD will provide" | Modern rendering of the Hebrew name-etymology |
| LOGOS | "The LORD will provide" | Same — all three agree |
| PNEUMA | "The LORD will provide" | Same |

**SOPHIA:** No divergence. All three render the place-name as "The LORD will provide" — the standard modern translation of YHWH-Yireh.

---

## 18:20 — Annual Moriah festival: "seven days"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "observed that festival with joy every year on this mountain — for seven days, eating and drinking" | "Every year" then "seven days" |
| LOGOS | "observed that festival with joy each year on that mountain for seven days — eating and drinking" | Same with slight restructuring |
| PNEUMA | "kept this as an annual celebration on that mountain — seven days of eating, drinking" | "Annual celebration" for "festival" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Festival" is the precise cultic term (Ge'ez 'ed / Hebrew hag). PNEUMA's "annual celebration" is natural but loses the cultic register of a pilgrimage festival.

---

## 18:21 — Mastema "ashamed" vs. "put to shame" vs. "humiliated"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he was ashamed" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "he was put to shame" | Passive: the outcome is imposed on him |
| PNEUMA | "he was humiliated" | Stronger emotional word |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Put to shame" captures both the passive (it is done to him by events) and the public/judicial dimension. EMET's "ashamed" is too internal/emotional. PNEUMA's "humiliated" is accurate but slightly over-translates.

---

**Total disagreements: 4 significant + 1 non-divergence**
